title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Falls 2.4% as Wall Street Slides (Nov 19)
summary: Tesla stock (TSLA) fell 2.43% to $374.41 on Nov 19 as Wall Street slid after Anthropic's debut, the day Tesla launched Cybercab in Dallas.
body_markdown:
## Why Tesla Stock Fell


Coverage of the session did not name a Tesla-specific reason for Thursday's drop, and the stock moved in step with the broader market. According to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) , the major averages fell to their session lows immediately after[Anthropic began trading](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-prices-83-raises-81-billion/) , as investors appeared to take profits at what CNBC called the culmination of a much-hyped moment for the AI trade. CNBC added that investors have grown more cautious on AI, focusing on whether heavy spending on the buildout will translate into meaningful profits, while AMD slid after Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position.


The day also brought company news. As reported by[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/tesla-expands-cybercab-dallas-first-195517775.html) , Tesla said on Thursday that it had launched Cybercab, its two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, in Dallas, its first expansion outside Austin, where the vehicle rolled out in September. Tesla already ran robotaxis in Dallas, but only with Model Y vehicles.


Separately, per[The Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/trump-just-disclosed-tesla-spacex-202931660.html) , the Office of Government Ethics released a transaction report on Thursday showing four Tesla purchases by President Donald Trump between Sept. 1 and Sept. 10, with a combined value in the range of $117,004 to $330,000. The author noted that the trades became public about eight weeks after they were made.


## TSLA Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Robotaxi rollout: according to Stocktwits, management said in October it aims to deliver Cybercabs to fleet customers by the end of this year, and the vehicle is priced at $29,990 for individuals, plus a $299 monthly autonomy subscription.
- Production plans: Stocktwits cited a report earlier this week of a €3 billion ($3.3 billion) investment in Tesla's German plant, adding a facility aimed at producing a million Cybercab units.


### Risks


- AI-trade caution: CNBC reported that investors are questioning whether heavy AI spending will turn into profits, a mood that sent all three major indices down more than 2% on Thursday.
- Weak trend: Stocktwits noted that TSLA has dropped 16% year-to-date, and Thursday's close came near the session low.
- Fleet ownership: Stocktwits reported that management expects "a vast majority" of Cybercabs to be Tesla-owned, and the Dallas launch adds a new vehicle to a city where Tesla already ran Model Y robotaxis.
